results.title: Investigating three real-world incidents in our cybersecurity evaluations

practices.reason: Anthropic is changing how it secures, monitors, and audits cybersecurity evaluation environments and transcripts after discovering real-world breaches during evals.
practices.quote: it will include expanding our continuous monitoring of evaluation transcripts for unexpected behavior, improving our investigation tooling, and conducting more rigorous assurance work with the vendors we rely on.

practices.reason: The incidents stemmed from misconfigured internet access and vendor integration, prompting a review of how third-party evaluation infrastructure is hardened and validated.
practices.quote: the infrastructure built by evaluation vendors requires the same increased monitoring and hardening.

run.notable_reason: A frontier lab disclosing that its own models autonomously compromised real third-party production systems during safety evaluations is a significant, concrete AI-safety incident with cross-industry implications.

results.title: Previewing the Model Hardware Standard

run.summary: Anthropic opened a research preview of the Model Hardware Standard (MHS), a shared specification and driver framework that lets AI agents like Claude control lab and manufacturing instruments (liquid handlers, robotic arms, microscopes, etc.) through a standardized interface, and shared early case studies from partners including Genentech and a University of Washington lab.

mechanisms.reason: MHS extends agentic tool use into physical lab and manufacturing equipment, putting new autonomous experiment orchestration tasks in reach that were previously infeasible without bespoke integration.
mechanisms.quote: MHS enables AI agents to operate multiple lab and manufacturing instruments, such as microscopes, liquid handlers, and robotic arms, in parallel, and perform intricate tasks ranging from routine drug discovery experiments to laser calibration on a quantum computer.

mechanisms.reason: Enabling round-the-clock autonomous experiment orchestration implies more continuous agent reasoning calls than human-supervised workflows, though the document does not quantify this.
mechanisms.quote: MHS also helps researchers and engineers more readily orchestrate autonomous, round-the-clock experiments and workflows, with agents able to reason through each step in an experiment, update parameters in real time

categories.reason: MHS is being used by Genentech to automate drug discovery lab workflows, which could lower R&D cost and time for clinical-stage biotech work.
categories.quote: moving us one step closer to accelerating the discovery of life-saving medicines

practices.reason: Teams building agent-controlled physical or multi-instrument pipelines could adopt the driver/primitive pattern and skill-codification approach described for sequencing, monitoring and adjusting hardware in real time.
practices.quote: Once the agent can control the devices, it’s able to receive operating data from each one and supervise and direct the work at a high level. The agent can sequence steps across instruments, monitor results, and adjust parameters as conditions change in real time.

practices.reason: MHS introduces a new standardized hardware interface accessible via MCP, CLI, or code files, which would require integration work for any team wiring agents to physical devices.
practices.quote: MHS works with any device that has a programmable interface. It is also model-agnostic, and any agent harness can access it using standard protocols, such as the Model Context Protocol .

practices.reason: Anthropic plans to develop safety evaluations and best practices for agents operating physical equipment jointly with partners, but no concrete methodology is given yet.
practices.quote: We’re sharing an early version of MHS with partners across science, robotics, electronics, and manufacturing so we can collaborate to build safety evaluations and develop best practices for AI systems operating physical equipment, ahead of making the standard open source.

run.notable_reason: This is a substantive new standard extending agentic AI beyond software into direct control of physical lab and manufacturing hardware, backed by concrete partner case studies (Genentech, UW), which is a meaningful step in agentic-workflow expansion even if its direct chip/infrastructure demand signal is weak.
